issues.legal_issue: Persons interested in a public trust are parties to a representative suit concerning the trust and may exercise rights conferred on parties by the resulting scheme decree.
material_facts: The original proceeding was brought under Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure to protect a public trust and resulted in a scheme decree for its administration.
The scheme decree gave the parties liberty to apply for further directions concerning administration of the trust.
The applicants were interested in the trust, although they were not named in the original suit title.
The applicants sought to challenge court orders permitting the sale of trust properties.
issues.conclusion: The applicants were parties to the representative suit in law and had locus standi to apply under the scheme decree; the lower courts erred in dismissing their application on the ground that they were not named in the original suit.
issues.legal_principle: A suit under Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure is a representative suit brought on behalf of all beneficiaries interested in a public trust. The reasoning in Raje Anandrao v. Shamrao and Ahmed Adam Sait v. Inayatullah Mekhri establishes that such a suit binds all interested persons, not only those named in the suit title. Explanation VI to Section 11 of the Code treats persons interested in the common public right as represented by those litigating bona fide on their behalf, including for purposes of constructive res judicata. A suit under Order I Rule 8 is similarly representative in nature.

predicates.section_92_trust_proceeding: The proceeding was brought representatively to protect the rights and administration of a public trust.
predicates.applicant_interested_in_trust: The applicant had an interest in the trust, even though the applicant was not named in the original suit.
predicates.scheme_permits_party_applications: The decree governing the trust allowed parties to seek further directions concerning its administration.

issues.definition: When a trust-protection proceeding is representative, an interested person may use the decree's application procedure if the decree permits such applications.

issues.legal_issue: A sale of public charitable trust property by private negotiation without public visibility and for less than market value should be set aside absent special reasons, and the property should be sold through a publicly advertised auction.
material_facts: Trustees obtained court permission to sell two trust properties through private negotiations.
The sales were conducted without newspaper publication or notice on the court notice board inviting the public to make offers.
The applicants alleged that the negotiated prices were about one-fifth of market value, and the Court was satisfied that the trust had not received market value.
Offers substantially above the prices paid had been made to the Court, supported by deposits.
issues.conclusion: The orders permitting the sales and the resulting sales were set aside. The properties were directed to be sold by public auction with wide publicity. The purchasers were entitled to repayment of the price with interest and compensation for superstructures and improvements, to be assessed by the subordinate court.
issues.legal_principle: Under Chenchu Ram Reddy v. Government of Andhra Pradesh, property of religious and charitable endowments must be jealously protected because the community has a beneficial interest in it. A private sale lacking public visibility, and liable to create public suspicion, should not be permitted unless special reasons justify it. The reserve price should be fixed after ascertaining market value to safeguard the endowment's interests.

rule.if: public_charitable_trust_property_sale and sale_by_private_negotiation and no_public_visibility and below_market_price and no_special_reason

predicates.public_charitable_trust_property_sale: The proceeding concerns the sale of property held by a public charitable or religious trust.
predicates.sale_by_private_negotiation: The trustees arranged the property sale through private negotiations rather than an open auction.
predicates.no_public_visibility: The sale process did not give the public meaningful notice or opportunity to compete.
predicates.below_market_price: The trust received a price below the property's market value.
predicates.no_special_reason: No special reason justified selling the property through private negotiations.

issues.definition: When trust property is privately sold without public visibility, below market value, and without special justification, the sale is set aside and an open public auction is ordered.
